# Lab-grown meat was supposed to save the world. What happened?

View image in fullscreen

A launch event for the world’s first lab-grown burger in London, 5 August 2013. Photograph: Toby Melville/Reuters

We were promised a panacea for the climate crisis and a way to save our food system. So why is nobody firing up the chicken vats? I went to find out

Erin Somers

Thu 5 Nov 2026 00.00 EST

Last modified on Wed 11 Nov 2026 06.34 EST

On 5 August 2013, a man and a woman ate a burger. Not just any burger: a world-historic burger, made from cattle cells grown in a laboratory by Mark Post, a professor of vascular physiology at Maastricht University in the Netherlands. The burger had taken two years to produce and cost €250,000 (about £210,000 at the time), money furnished by the Google co-founder Sergey Brin.
